what_it_is.prose: Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) is the Longueuil, Quebec-based gas-turbine subsidiary of Pratt & Whitney, a business of RTX Corporation. It designs and builds small and medium turboprop, turboshaft and turbofan engines, including the PW100/PW127 turboprop family. The PW127G variant powers the Airbus C-295, of which India has ordered 56 for the Indian Air Force (16 built in Spain and 40 assembled by Tata Advanced Systems at the Vadodara Final Assembly Line) — meaning P&WC engines are entering Indian military service. P&WC's India footprint centres on aftermarket support rather than manufacture: in July 2024 Pratt & Whitney opened a Customer Service Center in Bengaluru with more than 150 aerospace engineers to provide MRO support, spare-part management, engine leasing and reliability analysis for P&WC's roughly 68,000 engines in service worldwide, of which a large part of India's regional aviation fleet (ATR-72, ATR-42 and DHC-8-400 turboprops flown by IndiGo, Alliance Air, FLY91 and SpiceJet) is P&WC-powered. Trade reporting indicates the Tata Group and Airbus have studied local assembly of the PW127G at Vadodara to raise indigenous content on the C-295, but no P&WC manufacturing joint venture in India has been confirmed by a primary source. This dossier is scoped Tier B: a genuine but aftermarket-and-propulsion India footprint, without the manufacturing depth of a Tier A entity.

deployments_procurement.summary: P&WC's principal Indian defence relevance is as the engine OEM for the IAF's C-295 programme. The C-295 is powered by two PW127G turboprops; 56 aircraft were contracted in 2021 (₹21,935 crore), with 16 delivered fly-away from Airbus Seville and 40 to be assembled by Tata Advanced Systems in Vadodara — the first aircraft from the Indian line rolled out in 2026. On the civil/aftermarket side, P&WC deepened its India presence with the Bengaluru Customer Service Center (July 2024) and MRO agreements with Indian turboprop operators such as FLY91.

import_dependencies.summary: The PW127G is a fully imported, foreign-designed engine; India currently has no domestic design authority or licensed production for it. For the C-295, propulsion (P&WC, Canada), propeller systems and hot-section technology are sourced from the P&WC/RTX global supply chain, making the engine a 100% import-dependent element of an otherwise progressively indigenised airframe.

faq.question: What is Pratt & Whitney Canada's role in the Indian C-295 programme?
faq.answer: P&WC is the engine OEM for the Airbus C-295, which is powered by two PW127G turboprops. India has ordered 56 C-295s for the Indian Air Force (16 imported from Airbus Seville and 40 assembled by Tata Advanced Systems at Vadodara), so PW127G engines are entering Indian military service as part of that programme.

faq.question: Does Pratt & Whitney Canada manufacture engines in India?
faq.answer: Not confirmed. P&WC's India footprint is currently aftermarket and support: a Customer Service Center opened in Bengaluru in July 2024 (150+ engineers) providing MRO support, spares, leasing and reliability analysis, plus MRO deals with Indian turboprop operators such as FLY91. Trade reporting says the Tata Group and Airbus have studied local PW127G assembly at Vadodara, but no manufacturing joint venture has been confirmed by a primary source.
